must_fix.issue: A held question can wait forever when the `yourself` call W it names is queued on a promised answer A, and A is answered by a Return path that neither records A nor drains `pending_promises[A]`. W is then never replayed or failed, so W0 (the question whose takeFromOtherQuestion names W) gets no Return. Two paths do this. (1) `sendPrebuiltReturnFrame` with a non-results tag records nothing for A and drains nothing. HostPeer.respondHostCallException uses this path, so the WASM host ABI reaches it. (2) `sendReturnTakeFromOtherQuestion` and `sendReturnAcceptFromThirdParty` drain A's pipeline only when A itself is a marked `yourself` call. A plain A forwarded with translate_to_caller or sent_elsewhere never drains. On e9f37e1, W was not marked on arrival, so W0 got the bare redirect at once. W itself was stuck there too, so W's missing Return is pre-existing; W0's hang is new. There is a worse follow-on (probe A2). The stale `pending_promises[A]` bucket outlives Finish(A). When the remote reuses A's id for an unrelated call, that call's results replay W against the wrong target, and the held W0 silently gets W's results (n=42) as its RETURN results. On base, W0 had already got the bare tag.

must_fix.why: This breaks the invariant: W0 never gets a Return, only a cancel, deadline or disconnect ends it. C++ deadlocks with it, because it finishes W only after our Finish(W0). The C++ reference bounces every call pipelined on a question it sent us back as a tail call (Call(W, yourself, target = promisedAnswer(A)) + Return(W0, take W)). A WASM guest that answers A with an exception is ordinary use. The id-reuse follow-on turns the hang into a silent wrong value.

must_fix.issue: `sendPrebuiltReturnFrame` clears the `yourself` mark before its fallible steps (reserveResolvedAnswer and the send). Every other Return family clears it after a successful send. When the prebuilt Return is refused, the hold stays with no mark. A follow-up answer through the Peer's sendReturnException then takes the plain path. That path puts an exception Return for the tail call on the wire, which the C++ reference rejects. It never calls releaseHeldTailCall, so X waits for Finish(Y), which a compliant remote sends only after Finish(X). The refusal needs no OOM: reserveResolvedAnswer fails with PeerLimitExceeded when max_resolved_answers is full, and a remote can fill it with Finish-less calls (audit item 7). This is the only non-teardown place I found where the invariant 'a hold on Y implies Y's mark' breaks. A retry through HostPeer (respondHostCallException, which goes through prebuilt again) still releases the hold, so the hang needs a host that retries through the plain Peer API.

nice_to_have: Choke point. Two separate invariants carry the hold, and only one has a choke point. (a) 'A hold on Y implies Y's mark.' This can be made true by construction. Every place that ends Y's local state without a local answer removes the mark: clearSendResultsRouting in each Return family, finish.zig:37, the handleCall errdefer, and completeSelfLoopback*. Route every removal through one dropYourselfMark(Y, outcome). That function takes any hold on Y and queues its delivery (bare redirect, or tail_call_finished_reason) to run after the current send or at handleFrame exit, so no callback runs mid-send. It replaces settleTailCallOnFinish, releaseHeldTailCall and the late handleFinish errdefer, and it covers must-fix 2. The yourself-answer path keeps taking the hold before the send, as today. A forward back to the remote keeps Y marked, so noteYourselfCallForwarded must still release explicitly. (b) 'Y eventually gets a local terminal.' Here nothing is removed, so no removal hook can see it: Y stays marked and stuck (must-fix 1, and the OOM drops below). This needs either a drain rule (every Return for answer A that records neither a resolved nor a failed answer fails pending_promises[A]) or holding only Y states with a guaranteed terminal (dispatched, or parked on our promise export).

OOM-only waits (documented in general terms; no Return for X). Each one takes the hold, or leaves Y marked, before a fallible step, then swallows the error. (1) Frame build or decode in deliverHeldTailCall, settleTailCallOnFinish and releaseHeldTailCall: peer_return_send.zig:412-448. The H8 stack-buffer pattern from deliverLocalException would make these infallible. (2) failQueuedPromisedCalls when it cannot seed its worklist (:752), and its NoDrain send errors (:770). (3) answerDroppedParkedCall send errors: peer_export_release.zig:488. (4) The replay drains `continue` on decode errors with no Return: src/rpc/promises/pending_calls.zig:204-212 and :253-262. pending_call.question_id is already known, so they could still answer. (5) The relay callbacks swallow a failed sendReturnResults build: peer_cross_peer_proxy.zig:331 and mod.zig:2624. A cross-peer clone can fail without OOM, so this one is not purely OOM.

handleFinish still registers `errdefer self.settleTailCallOnFinish(qid)` at mod.zig:4900, after `_ = try self.cancelQueuedPendingQuestion(...)` at :4866. That call has already dropped Y's mark through sendReturnTag(.canceled), which skips releaseHeldTailCall by design. The same applies to the handleCall errdefer at peer_call_inbound.zig:145, which removes the mark without settling. Both errors leave handleFrame, and native conn.zig:333-337 and the transport callbacks then close the connection, so X is settled by the disconnect. Still, register the errdefer first; settleTailCallOnFinish is idempotent.

Conclusion on the lens: the hold settles on every path where Y is answered, refused, finished, released, forwarded back or torn down, except refused prebuilt sends (must-fix 2) and OOM. It does not settle when Y is marked but stuck on an answer whose pipeline is never drained (must-fix 1). That case is a liveness regression and, with id reuse, a silent wrong value. A single mark-removal choke point can enforce 'hold implies mark'. Liveness of Y needs a separate drain rule. The propagate instance is new with 34efe40; before it, the stale forwarded_questions entry leaked for the Peer's lifetime instead. The wire effect is benign: C++ silently ignores a Finish for an unknown id. Suggested fix, for all modes: skip the registration in forwardResolvedCall when `!self.questions.contains(forwarded_question_id)`.

The connection stays up, so the remote's question entry for Y leaks until it closes.

Functional divergence from C++, unchanged from main: when C++ forwards a call it received with `sendResultsTo = yourself`, directTailCall skips the same-connection tail call because redirectResults is set (rpc.c++:3378). It does a plain `send()` and copies the results into the redirected response (:3416-3431), so the tail-calling question X gets the real results. capnp-zig forwards the call with `yourself` again (propagate mode), so X gets only the bare redirect (native: `unfollowed_tail_call_reason`). Suggested change: forward a marked call in a caller/translate-style mode and answer Y through sendReturnResults. The held X would then get its results, and the remote would not need to keep the forwarded call's answer.

Stale stash, unchanged from main: a capnp-zig remote that receives the forwarded `yourself` call Y' answers it and stashes its results. No redirect ever names Y'. The entry is freed only when the id is reused, which never happens soon because capnp-zig question ids are monotonic, or at deinit. A long-lived Zig-to-Zig connection can therefore fill `max_loopback_result_stash` (4096), after which genuine tail calls answered before their redirect degrade to the bare tag. 7004322 now argues that the redirect always precedes the call's Finish, so freeing a still-kept stash entry at that Finish would be safe.

Doc nit (7004322, src/rpc/peer/mod.zig:776-782): 'the C++ reference finishes its tail call only after the question's Finish' holds only while promise pipelining is on. If the tail request carries noPromisePipelining (callNoIntercept copies it, rpc.c++:1113), tailSend gives the pipeline no QuestionRef (:2604-2606). The QuestionRef then drops at once, and the wire order is Call(Y), Finish(Y), Return(X, takeFromOtherQuestion=Y). The id-reuse drop is still safe, because the redirect precedes any reuse, but the sentence overstates the ordering.

Finish(Y) then finds no pending Y' and drains nothing. So the call waits until disconnect, as the skipped-record degrade says.

repair.safety_net:
The net is tied to one thing: the call's `yourself` mark (src/rpc/peer/return/peer_return_send.zig). holdTailCall holds only a call that is marked, not forwarded, and not stuck in a queue on an answer that already returned. Every removal of the mark goes through ReturnSend.dropYourselfMark, which ends any hold on the call with the bare takeFromOtherQuestion, as before holds existed.

Where the mark is removed:
- clearSendResultsRouting, which every Return family runs after its send (sendPrebuiltReturnFrame now does it after the send and the commit).
- The Finish ops (`.remove_send_results_to_yourself = ReturnSendImpl.dropYourselfMark` in mod.zig).
- The handleCall errdefer (peer_call_inbound.zig).
- noteSendResultsToThirdParty (peer_third_party_routes.zig).

Two paths take the hold themselves instead of releasing it:
- The call's own answer uses takeYourselfMark, which takes the mark and the hold together.
- handleFinish takes the hold before anything can drop the mark, and settles it with tail_call_finished_reason, also through an errdefer.

The per-path releaseHeldTailCall calls in the prebuilt, tag, take and accept sends are removed. noteYourselfCallForwarded still releases explicitly, because a forwarded call keeps its mark.

All delivery goes through one function, deliverHeldTailCall. If the real terminal cannot be built or delivered and the question is still open (and not held again), it delivers the bare redirect. That frame is built and decoded in a 4096-byte stack buffer, using the heap only past it (deliverSyntheticTailReturn). completeSelfLoopbackException also falls back to the bare redirect when it cannot build its exception frame. So once the answer path is entered, a held question always gets exactly one Return.

Tests are in tests/rpc/peer/rpc_reflected_direct_handler_test.zig:
- A prebuilt Return refused by the max_resolved_answers budget (rewritten in commit 2 to check the must-fix-2 outcome).
- Five one-allocation-failure sweeps over the end of the named call: results, exception, prebuilt, the remote's Finish, and the Release of a promise export. A transport close follows any error that escapes handleFrame.
- A test that both synthetic frames build and decode over std.testing.failing_allocator.

new_regressions.issue: New hang compared with main. A held tail call gets no Return, and a graceful shutdown never completes, when the named yourself call Y is a streaming call queued behind a deferred streaming call. The stream drain (stream_dispatch.zig:185, `!peer.is_shutting_down`) stops dispatching queued streaming calls once shutdown starts. So Y is marked, not forwarded and not stuck on a returned answer, and holdTailCall holds X on it. After that nothing answers Y. The remote finishes Y only after X's Finish, so this is a deadlock. With the bare Peer default (`shutdown_drain_timeout_ms = null`, no call deadline) it never ends. With the 5 s drain bound that TCP and native use, X ends at the bound with 'peer shutting down' and the shutdown waits until then. On main X gets the bare takeFromOtherQuestion at the redirect, and the shutdown completes at once. The same root cause also applies when Y is a plain call queued in pending_promises on a streaming call that is stuck in the stream queue.

new_regressions.issue: Remote-forceable CPU amplification. holdTailCall runs stuckOnReturnedAnswer for every takeFromOtherQuestion Return that names a marked call. The walk does up to pending_promises.count() hops, and each hop runs queuedOnAnswer, a full scan of every queued call. That is O(chain x queued calls) per redirect, and it runs before the hold-table-full check. A remote can build a chain of about 4000 pipelined calls (each on the previous answer, the head waiting on our host) within the default limits. Then every redirect for one of our outstanding questions costs about 19 ms in ReleaseFast (438 ms in Debug). The same redirect with no chain costs 0.86 us, and on main it is O(1) at about 0.5 ms Debug at any chain length. forwardedToRemote adds a further O(forwarded_questions) scan per redirect.
